sentences.text: Sutterella is a genus of bile-resistant, microaerophilic, Gram-negative bacteria.
The genus was proposed for unusual bile-resistant clinical isolates obtained primarily from appendiceal and peritoneal fluid specimens, which 16S rRNA data showed were not Campylobacter.
A review describes Sutterella as showing pro-inflammatory properties, inducing cytokines such as IL-6 and TNF, and degrading immunoglobulin A, while also inducing anti-inflammatory IL-10.
The same review reports that in Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease its abundance correlates with disease severity and markers such as amyloid burden and oxidative stress.
Sutterella wadsworthensis has been reported to encode an immunoglobulin A protease digesting human IgA1 and IgA2 but not mouse IgA, detectable in individuals globally.
